problems.description: package.json declares bin 'dist/cli.js' and build script 'tsc', but no tsconfig.json appears in the diff — without rootDir/outDir config the build won't emit src/cli.ts to dist/cli.js, so the published bin path and 'npm run build' are likely broken.
Mechanical analysis reports 30 convention violations (score 0.54): snake_case functions, non-UPPER_CASE constants, and PascalCase class/interface infractions in cli.ts, config.ts, and dev-server.ts.
Cognitive complexity +32 across the 8 new functions — the template-literal rendering (renderPage/renderIndex) and parseArguments loop are more convoluted than needed for a small SSG.
Hand-rolls an escapeHtml helper instead of relying on the already-imported marked/gray-matter stack, duplicating common utility logic.
Package name 'ssg' and generic bin are weakly namespaced; fine for a scaffold but the identity no longer reflects the deleted Todo-API seed it replaced.
Smells +3 flagged by SonarQube (mechanical); severity unverified against the truncated diff.

strengths: Clean modular separation: thin cli.ts entry point delegating to a library-style site.ts (render/markdown/options concerns split out).
Proper testing infrastructure configured up front: jest + ts-jest preset with an explicit tests/ testMatch convention.
Story-appropriate greenfield rebuild — replaces the mismatched Express Todo-API seed with an SSG that matches the static_site_gen story description and dependencies (gray-matter, marked).
Zero new bugs and zero duplications per SonarQube delta.
commit_reviews.summary: A structurally sound greenfield SSG rebuild that fits the story's CLI architecture and wires in testing, but convention adherence is dragged to 0.54 by 30 reported violations and a missing tsconfig risks a broken dist bin path — though the listed cli.ts violations (snake_case functions, non-UPPER_CASE constants) do not appear in the visible cli.ts diff, which uses PascalCase interfaces and camelCase functions, suggesting analyzer noise or infractions concentrated in unshown files (config.ts, dev-server.ts).

problems.description: createRenderer detects the layouts/partials subdirectories by string-matching relative(path).split(sep)[0], which is fragile (breaks on root-level files colliding with those names and is hard to read). A traversal that filters on entry.isDirectory() while recursing would be cleaner. This is consistent with the +35 cognitive complexity delta measured by SonarQube.

Layouts receive both `content` (rendered markdown) and `body` (template output) with different meanings, and templates receive `content` but not `body`; the dual-purpose field naming on the same Page object is confusing API design that will be easy to misuse.

The mechanical convention score (0.54) is driven by violations in cli.ts, config.ts, and dev-server.ts (PascalCase classes/interfaces, UPPER_CASE constants, snake_case functions) — but the diff only touches cli.ts/site.ts/tests, and the listed cli.ts rules appear to be false positives for a TypeScript file (no classes/constants/snake_case in it). The violations appear pre-existing, not introduced by this commit.

Page markdown is passed to templates as `content: page.html`; Handlebars escapes `{{content}}` by default, so authors must remember triple-stash `{{{content}}}` to emit HTML — a silent no-output trap rather than a vulnerability, but worth documenting.

strengths: Fully backward compatible: default templatesDir and graceful fallbacks to renderArticle/renderPage when no templates or default layout exist
Mirrors existing patterns, e.g. templateFiles recursion parallels markdownFiles, and BuildOptions/error-message style ('does not exist') extend consistently
Isolated Handlebars instance via Handlebars.create() avoids global registration pollution
Tests added covering template + layout + partials rendering
Clear errors for missing templates/layouts, and .hbs extension normalization applied uniformly in both frontmatter and template file names
commit_reviews.summary: A well-scoped, backward-compatible templating feature that respects the SSG's existing file-discovery and options patterns, with minor structural complexity debt (string-based directory skipping, dual content/body semantics) that the measured +35 cognitive complexity supports.

problems.description: The build closure in server.ts references webSocketServer and server before their const declarations (TDZ), relying on call ordering (ignoreInitial chokidar) to avoid a runtime error; fragile to future refactors.
Chokidar triggers a full buildSite + reload broadcast on every event with no debounce; rapid multi-file save bursts cause rebuild thrash.
New dev server tests cover only basic file serving; no coverage for the WebSocket upgrade path, path-traversal 403, 404, or close().

Mechanical convention score 0.54 (30 violations); new code flags Constants should be UPPER_CASE (reloadScript, contentTypes). Discrepancy: listed violations reference config.ts and dev-server.ts, which are not part of this diff, and cli.ts has no classes/interfaces, so the score appears inflated by pre-existing or misattributed files.
Reload script is injected as a single inline string constant into HTML; adequate for a dev server but couples server output to a hand-maintained script fragment.

strengths: Feature cleanly scoped into src/server.ts, reusing buildSite and BuildOptions and returning a DevelopmentServer interface, honoring the existing module structure.
CLI refactor replaces the bare-else option branch with explicit per-option handling (fixing --templates assignment) and adds integer/range validation for --port.
Path-traversal protection via resolve + outputDir prefix check before serving files.
Live reload implemented with a noServer WebSocketServer scoped to /__ssg_reload, avoiding interception of unrelated upgrade requests.
Integration tests added using real node:http requests against the running server.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-scoped, convention-consistent dev-server feature that reuses the existing build pipeline and adds real tests, with minor debt in un-debounced rebuilds, TDZ-fragile closure ordering, and thin coverage of the reload/path-safety paths.

problems.description: src/config.ts:loadTypeScriptModule monkey-patches the deprecated require.extensions['.ts'] hook AND evals transpiled source via new Function. This is fragile, globally mutates the module system, and destroys stack traces/source maps for config errors. A proper loader (jiti/tsx/esbuild) or native TS node would be more robust; the +20 cognitive complexity and a portion of the +4 smells concentrate here.

src/plugins/dev-server.ts imports IncomingMessage, Server, ServerResponse as value imports instead of import type; under verbatimModuleSyntax/isolatedModules this fails compilation. Related: loadTypeScriptModule is snake_case, matching the analyzer's 'Functions should not use snake_case' flag.

src/plugins/dev-server.ts declares `let webSocketServer` without an initializer while the `build` closure dereferences it; correctness depends on the ordering where WebSocketServer is assigned before the chokidar watcher is created. Any future reorder introduces a TypeError, and the current buildSite call is duplicated (direct call plus the closure) rather than routed through `build`.

The refactor introduces a new Plugin contract (onStart/onFile) and a config loader with zero tests in the diff; the onFile/onStart lifecycle and the require.extensions hook restoration are exactly the kind of behavior that breaks silently.

Running the user config through new Function is acceptable for a trusted local ssg.config.ts, but it bypasses Node module caching and debugger tooling; worth an explicit note if config is ever loaded from untrusted paths.

strengths: Clean plugin architecture (Plugin interface + MarkdownPlugin/DevServerPlugin) that reuses existing Page/BuildOptions/BuildContext types from site.ts rather than inventing parallel abstractions.
dev-server.ts implements correct path-traversal protection (403 when the resolved path escapes outputDir) and a working hot-reload via WebSocket with graceful close() lifecycle.
The try/finally restoration of require.extensions is correct under exceptions, avoiding leaked module-system hooks.
SonarQube reports 0 bugs and 0.0% duplication, and the plugin extraction net-reduces 238 lines while keeping the core site.ts surface unchanged.
commit_reviews.summary: A genuinely useful modularization (plugin API + extracted markdown/dev-server) that respects existing types, but the require.extensions/new Function config loader and an ordering-fragile dev-server closure add real technical debt (0.54 convention score is roughly right, though the analyzer's listed 'Classes should use PascalCase' violations are false positives — DevServerPlugin/MarkdownPlugin are correctly PascalCased).

problems.description: buildSite() public return type is augmented to `Page[] & { stats }`, an array-with-extra-property trick that changes the API contract for every caller (including the dev server) and requires them to know about `.stats`; a `{ pages, stats }` result object would be idiomatic.

Cache read/write/invalidation logic is embedded monolithically in buildSite() with tangled conditionals (`incremental && !clean` vs `useCache || clean || !incremental`) instead of using the existing plugin hook seam, matching the +34 cognitive complexity and +1 smell delta.
CachedPage stores `page: { ...page, sourcePath: undefined }` to drop the absolute path — an undefined-typed field hack that is fragile if cache entries are consumed elsewhere.

Every build still sha256-hashes all source files and all template files to decide skips, so the 'incremental' speedup only avoids plugin rendering, not file I/O; the skip path also caches duplicate `page.html` alongside `renderedHtml`.
No tests accompany the incremental/clean semantics despite cache invalidation and template-hash logic being subtle.

strengths: Versioned and path-validated cache (version, contentDir, outputDir, templatesDir) reduces risk of stale builds
Sensible invalidation semantics: cache auto-expires on directory or template-hash change and `--clean` forces a full rebuild
Incremental flow reuses the existing plugin hooks (onFile/afterBuild) and maintains camelCase naming consistent with the surrounding file
SonarQube reports no new bugs and no duplications
commit_reviews.summary: A useful incremental-build feature with sound cache validation, but it lands as a debt-accumulating monolith that hacks buildSite's return type and bypasses the plugin seam rather than composing with the existing architecture.

compounding_issues: The seed codebase (an Express Todo API) is unrelated to static site generation and was discarded wholesale in Session 1; the story's first commit is a full replacement rather than an evolution, so the seed provided no carryover value and set the project's convention baseline at 0.51 (snake_case functions, non-PascalCase classes/interfaces) that never recovered

Session 4's loadPlugins mutates the global require.extensions['.ts'] loader as a temporary monkey-patch; the global state makes concurrent/parallel builds unsafe and is a latent hazard carried into Session 5

Session 5's incremental cache is wired only to the `build` command; the `serve` watcher from Session 3 still calls a full buildSite() on every change, so the caching win never reaches the dev-loop workflow

Session 5 computes the plugin portion of the render hash by serializing plugin functions with String() — a fragile proxy for plugin identity that misses behavior changes not reflected in function source
key_decisions: Discard the Express/Todo seed and greenfield a strict TypeScript static site generator (gray-matter frontmatter + marked rendering + generated index) instead of extending the seeded app

Adopt Handlebars for templating with layouts, partials, frontmatter-selected templates, and strict path-traversal guards (isWithin + .hbs extension whitelist) — explicit security hardening in Session 2
Build the dev server on node:http with chokidar watching and WebSocket live-reload rather than pulling in an HTTP framework

Extract the growing monolith into a plugin architecture in Session 4: Plugin interface with lifecycle hooks (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) plus on-demand ssg.config.ts transpilation; src/index.ts shrank 234→127 lines
Implement incremental builds keyed by sha256 render hashes that correctly fold in template, layout, partial, and plugin dependencies, plus build statistics (Session 5)
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily and monotonically across the five sessions despite a rocky start. Session 1 greenfielded a clean, fully-tested core (the one regressive commit, flagged 'worse' for deleting the 106-line seed wholesale and shipping 46 convention violations); Session 2 added templating with security hardening ('better'); Session 3 integrated a live-reloading dev server with correct HTTP semantics ('better'). Session 4 was structurally mixed — the plugin refactor hit its architectural target but moved metrics the wrong way for a refactor commit (+13 cognitive complexity, +2.7% duplication, 'worse') — while Session 5 capped the arc with a dependency-aware incremental cache ('better'), the only session to introduce a SonarQube bug (+1). Test coverage grew monotonically at every step (119 → 199 → 285 → 372 → 483 lines) with no session forcing rework of a prior decision, though the convention score stayed flat at 0.513 throughout, indicating the naming debt seeded in Session 1 was never addressed.
story_review.summary: A highly coherent five-session arc that took a discarded Todo-API seed to a plugin-based, incrementally-caching, live-reload static site generator, with quality and test coverage improving monotonically and only minor residual warts (global loader monkey-patch, full-rebuild serve watcher, flat convention score).
